_README: Rules used when a farmer reads out the levels (low / medium / high) from their Soil Health Card. Every rule below is taken from a source note that is ALREADY in fertilizers.json (ICAR-IISS Bhopal district-wise recommendations), nothing is invented. 'action' is 'skip' (leave that nutrient out) or 'reduce' (cut it by 'percent'). Only phosphorus rules exist, because those are the only card-based rules in the data so far. To add a rule for nitrogen or potash, add an entry here ONLY after finding it in an ICAR or PAU document, and write that document in 'source'. A farmer's card values that match no rule are noted on screen, but the amounts do not change.

rules.text: Your Soil Health Card shows {level} phosphorus, so DAP is left out for this crop (ICAR: in medium-to-high phosphorus soils, phosphorus can be skipped for the kharif crop).
Your Soil Health Card shows {level} phosphorus, so DAP is left out for this crop (ICAR: in medium-to-high phosphorus soils, phosphorus can be skipped for the kharif crop).

Your Soil Health Card shows high phosphorus, so DAP is left out and the urea is increased to make up the nitrogen that DAP would have given (ICAR: in high phosphorus soils, phosphorus can be skipped for 2 to 3 years).
Your Soil Health Card shows high phosphorus, so the phosphorus (DAP) is reduced by 25% (ICAR: in high phosphorus soils, reduce the phosphorus dose by 25%).
